projects.title: PhD Thesis: Human Posture and Motion Prediction
projects.tagline: Six papers. One question: can simulation tools predict how real humans move in real vehicles? Here is what I found.
projects.summary: Five years of interconnected research on whether automotive DHM tools can be made reliable enough to replace or delay expensive physical prototyping. Six papers, from practitioner interviews to 1-million-run optimization frameworks to validated motion prediction models.
projects.challenge: DHM tools are standard in automotive engineering, but practitioners were losing time to manual corrections, inaccurate posture predictions, and workflows that did not connect digital simulation to real human behaviour. Nobody had done a systematic, evidence-based study of where exactly the tools were failing or what it would take to fix them.
projects.solution: A six-paper research programme moving from practitioner reality through method development to model validation and improvement.
whatIDid: Started by interviewing 10 expert ergonomics designers from 7 Swedish automotive companies to map where current tools were failing before building anything
Developed the Body Shape Alignment procedure that standardized how digital manikins are seated in vehicle models, later used in 3 subsequent studies
Built an automated multi-objective optimization framework running over 1 million simulation configurations to identify interior layouts that work for all body types
Compared competing posture prediction methods against real-world data from 199 Volvo drivers across two vehicle types, giving practitioners a clear decision rule
Created stature-based posture strategies that improved prediction accuracy for short drivers by 37% using existing OEM test data
Developed and validated a new heuristic motion prediction method (SFM) with 11x lower velocity error than the existing standard
impact: 6 peer-reviewed publications, 145 total citations, h-index 8
Practitioners now have evidence-based guidance: which posture method for which vehicle type, and how to feed existing data back into simulation tools
The alignment procedure from Paper B became the standardized foundation for 3 subsequent studies
Posture prediction accuracy for short drivers improved from 36.4 mm to 22.9 mm RMSE (37% reduction)
projects.learning: Research that starts by listening to practitioners before building anything solves problems that actually matter. Every technical contribution in this thesis traced directly back to a gap confirmed by people doing the work in industry.

projects.title: Mapped Where Simulation Tools Were Failing Practitioners
projects.tagline: Before building better tools, I interviewed the people using them. Every single expert confirmed the same four problems.
projects.summary: A structured qualitative study with 10 expert ergonomics designers from 7 Swedish automotive OEMs and suppliers, mapping end-to-end workflows, tool usage patterns, and the pain points that mattered most.
projects.challenge: Swedish automotive OEMs were investing in DHM tools but had no evidence-based picture of how ergonomics designers actually used them, where the tools were failing, and what was really needed. Tool improvements were being driven by assumptions rather than practitioner reality.
projects.solution: Semi-structured expert interviews with systematic qualitative content analysis to map workflows and identify the gaps that mattered most.
whatIDid: Designed and ran 10 semi-structured expert interviews (60 to 75 minutes each) with ergonomics designers from 7 OEMs and suppliers
Built a structured qualitative coding framework to categorize findings across workflow stages, tool usage, pain points, and future needs
Mapped the full ergonomics workflow from requirements definition through validation, identifying where each type of tool was used and where it broke down
impact: All 10 participants independently confirmed: DHM tools were slow, hard to use, and produced inaccurate posture predictions requiring manual correction
Identified 4 concrete research gaps confirmed by every expert: human behaviour prediction, tool usability, ergonomics evaluation methods, and system integration
These findings directly shaped the technical research agenda for Papers B through F
Published at DESIGN 2022, one of the leading international design research conferences
projects.learning: Industry practitioners are the best research compass. When all 10 experts independently name the same 4 problems, those are the 4 problems worth solving.

projects.title: Fixed the Starting Point of Every Seated Driving Simulation
projects.tagline: Digital manikins were floating in space because the vehicle reference point does not match the human hip joint. I built the procedure to fix that.
projects.summary: The SAE J826 H-point does not correspond to the human anatomical hip joint, and there was no standardized procedure to bridge the gap. This caused non-reproducible seated posture setups that depended on who was running the simulation.
projects.challenge: Before any driving posture simulation can begin, the digital manikin has to be seated in the vehicle correctly. The standard vehicle reference point (the H-point) does not correspond to the human anatomical hip joint, and no standardized method existed to bridge the gap. Engineers were manually adjusting alignment by feel, producing results that depended on which engineer was running the simulation. The mismatch was largest for high-BMI body types.
projects.solution: The Body Shape Alignment (BSA) procedure: place a virtual H-point Machine template at the vehicle seat reference point, align its geometry to the seat surface, then align the manikin body mesh to the template.
whatIDid: Developed the Body Shape Alignment (BSA) procedure using a virtual H-point Machine template to anchor manikin positioning to vehicle seat geometry
Tested BSA across 14 digital manikins spanning the full BMI range from the CAESAR anthropometric database, including both male and female bodies
Compared BSA head-to-head against the existing Statistical Prediction Method (SPM) in a Volkswagen Beetle CAD model using 3D body meshes
impact: SPM produced physically unrealistic floating positions for high-BMI manikins (detaching forward from the seat surface), requiring manual correction every time
BSA maintained consistent, realistic seat contact across all 14 manikins regardless of body type
BSA became the standardized alignment step for Papers C, D, and E, providing a reproducible foundation across the full research programme
projects.learning: Unsexy infrastructure fixes are often the highest-leverage technical contributions. If the starting conditions of a simulation are wrong and non-reproducible, no amount of sophisticated modelling downstream will correct that.

projects.title: Replaced Manual Trial-and-Error with 1 Million Automated Simulations
projects.tagline: Vehicle interior ergonomics is an optimization problem. I built the framework that treats it like one.
projects.summary: Built an automated multi-objective optimization pipeline coupling NSGA-II with IPS IMMA DHM software to systematically explore interior layout options for a diverse driver population.
projects.challenge: Designing a vehicle interior that works ergonomically for drivers of all body sizes involves balancing 5 design variables against 4 geometric constraints for 14 anthropometric profiles simultaneously. Engineers were solving this through manual trial and error, one configuration at a time. Too slow to explore the real design space and too subjective to produce traceable results.
projects.solution: Coupled the NSGA-II genetic algorithm with IPS IMMA to automate the search for Pareto-optimal interior layouts across a diverse manikin population.
whatIDid: Built an automated optimization pipeline coupling the NSGA-II genetic algorithm with IPS IMMA DHM software

Defined 5 design variables (seat and steering wheel positions), 4 geometric hard constraints (head, knee, thigh clearances and vision angle), and a joint-angle-based ergonomic objective for 14 digital human manikins
Ran 1,000 optimization iterations, each evaluating 75 posture configurations across 14 manikins, for a total of over 1 million individual simulation runs
impact: Algorithm converged at approximately 550 iterations, identifying a Pareto-optimal design achieving only 38 unacceptable joint angles across the full 14-manikin population
All 4 geometric hard constraints satisfied by the selected solution
Demonstrated that automated systematic exploration identifies solutions manual iteration would never reach in a practical project timeline
Published in International Journal of Industrial Ergonomics (2025)
projects.learning: Once a design problem can be expressed as objectives and constraints, automation almost always outperforms human trial and error in both speed and solution quality. The leverage is in the formulation, not in running the algorithm.

projects.title: Tested Two Prediction Models Against 199 Real Drivers
projects.tagline: Which DHM posture prediction method is actually more accurate? The answer depends on which vehicle you are designing.
projects.summary: The first rigorous head-to-head comparison of the two main driving posture prediction approaches, evaluated against real preferred-position data from 199 drivers in two Volvo vehicles with different seat height configurations.
projects.challenge: Automotive engineers use DHM tools daily to predict where drivers will position their seats, steering wheels, and eye height during vehicle design. Two main prediction approaches exist, but nobody had tested them head-to-head against a large real-world dataset across multiple vehicle types. Engineers were choosing methods based on habit, not evidence.
projects.solution: Collected real preferred-position data from 199 drivers across two Volvo vehicles and compared both methods using RMSE, MAE, correlation, and Bland-Altman analysis.
whatIDid: Analyzed real preferred-position data from 199 drivers in two Volvo vehicles with different seat height configurations (low-seat SUV and high-seat model)
Compared the Statistical Prediction Method (regression-based) against the Optimization Prediction Method (comfort-maximization) for H-point, eye-point, and steering wheel positions
Applied RMSE, MAE, Pearson correlation, and Bland-Altman analysis, introducing Bland-Altman plots to this research domain for the first time
impact: OPM outperformed for fore-aft H-point in both vehicles (47.2 mm vs 48.8 mm RMSE in Vehicle A; 48.5 mm vs 59.9 mm in Vehicle B)
SPM outperformed for vertical H-point in both vehicles (23.4 mm vs OPM 26.0 mm in Vehicle A)
Both methods underperformed for short and tall drivers, pointing directly to the next research question addressed in Paper E
Bland-Altman analysis revealed systematic prediction biases invisible to RMSE metrics alone
projects.learning: In most real prediction problems, no single model wins everywhere. The most useful output is often a clear decision rule: use this method for this context, use that one for that one.

projects.title: Turned Unused OEM Test Data into a 37% Accuracy Improvement
projects.tagline: OEM posture clinic data is usually left unused. I built the pipeline that feeds it back into DHM tools and improved prediction for extreme body sizes by up to 37%.
projects.summary: A three-step pipeline to connect real OEM posture clinic data to DHM prediction models, improving accuracy for short and tall drivers by creating stature-based strategies from 49 real participants without a dedicated new study.
projects.challenge: DHM tools apply a single generic posture strategy to all drivers regardless of body size. Short and tall drivers consistently get the worst predictions. Meanwhile, most automotive OEMs routinely collect driver posture data in test clinics that sits unused and disconnected from their simulation models.
projects.solution: A three-step pipeline: measure real preferred positions, generate individualized manikins, simulate at measured positions to extract joint angles, then build stature-based strategies.
whatIDid: Built a 3-step pipeline to feed real driver data back into DHM prediction: measure preferred positions from 49 Volvo Cars drivers, generate individualized manikins in IPS IMMA, simulate each manikin at their measured position to extract representative joint angles
Derived 3 stature-based posture strategies (short, medium, tall) from the extracted data
Compared stature-based strategies against the default generic Seated Car strategy using RMSE for H-point and eye-point positions
impact: H-point vertical RMSE improved from 36.4 mm to 22.9 mm for short drivers (37% reduction)
Eye-point vertical RMSE improved from 32.3 mm to 22.8 mm for short drivers and from 27.1 mm to 22.9 mm for tall drivers
Demonstrated that existing OEM test clinic data at 49 participants is sufficient to improve simulation accuracy without a dedicated new study
Presented at the 22nd IEA World Congress (2024)
projects.learning: Many organisations sit on data that could improve their models. Connecting existing data assets to the tools that need them is often higher value than collecting new data from scratch.

projects.title: New Motion Model Cuts Velocity Prediction Error by 11x
projects.tagline: Built a new heuristic prediction method for 3D reaching motions that outperforms the optimization-based standard by 11x on velocity accuracy.
projects.summary: Developed and validated a new heuristic prediction method (Steering-FABRIK Method) for upper-extremity reaching motions in 3D space, and introduced a dual-metric evaluation framework combining RMSE and Dynamic Time Warping.
projects.challenge: DHM tools predict how drivers reach for in-vehicle controls, but existing optimization-based methods require complete task specification upfront, are computationally expensive, and produce average trajectories that do not capture real human variability. There was also no established evaluation framework that treated path accuracy, velocity accuracy, and joint angle accuracy as separate performance dimensions.
projects.solution: The Steering-FABRIK Method (SFM) combining a 3D steering dynamics model, adaptive velocity modelling, and FABRIK inverse kinematics, evaluated with a novel dual-metric RMSE plus DTW framework.
whatIDid: Developed the Steering-FABRIK Method (SFM): combined a 3D steering dynamics model, adaptive velocity model, and FABRIK inverse kinematics into a single prediction pipeline
Captured and analyzed 120 real reaching motion sequences (10 participants, 4 reaching tasks, 3 trials each) using an 8-camera optical motion capture system
Compared SFM head-to-head against the optimization-based method (OPM) using a dual-metric evaluation framework combining RMSE and Dynamic Time Warping (DTW)
impact: SFM reduced peak velocity prediction error from 31.6 cm/s (OPM) to 2.8 cm/s, an 11-fold improvement in velocity accuracy
SFM outperformed on path accuracy for 3 of 4 tasks (Task 1 path RMSE: 23.4 cm vs 31.3 cm for OPM)
OPM outperformed on joint angle accuracy (10.8 degrees vs 12.8 degrees RMSE), establishing a clear use-case split between the two methods
DTW analysis revealed systematic model behaviours that RMSE missed entirely, establishing a better evaluation practice
projects.learning: How you evaluate a model determines what you learn about it. RMSE alone masked critical differences that DTW revealed. Better always has to be answered relative to a specific purpose.

evidence.publicationTitle: Predicting Human Upper Extremity Reaching Motions: Comparison of Optimization-based Method and Heuristic Method

projects.title: Ground-Truth Validation from 199 Drivers and Motion Capture
projects.tagline: High-quality experimental datasets from real vehicles and optical motion capture, used to test simulation tools against actual human behaviour.
projects.summary: Experimental infrastructure work: designing and executing two validation studies that generated ground-truth data for benchmarking posture and motion prediction models against real human behaviour.
projects.challenge: Simulation methods for human posture and motion prediction are only credible if tested against real measured behaviour. Most DHM research shortcuts this step or validates against small or low-quality datasets, which understates how poorly current tools perform and where they fail.
projects.solution: Designed and executed two rigorous validation studies providing the ground-truth datasets for Papers D and F.
whatIDid: Designed experimental protocols for two validation studies: in-vehicle driving posture with 199 real Volvo drivers across two vehicle types, and upper-extremity reaching with 10 participants using an 8-camera optical motion capture system
Applied RMSE, DTW, Pearson correlation, and Bland-Altman analysis to compare simulation outputs against measured ground truth
Standardized data processing pipelines to ensure reproducibility across studies and research institutions
impact: Generated the ground-truth datasets enabling rigorous head-to-head comparison of competing prediction models in Papers D and F
First application of Bland-Altman analysis to DHM posture prediction, revealing systematic biases hidden by standard RMSE metrics
Datasets remain available for future model development and benchmarking without additional participant recruitment
projects.learning: Good validation data is a multiplier. The same experimental dataset powered multiple independent research questions and will continue to be useful long after the original study is complete.

evidence.notes: Experimental datasets used to validate seated posture and reaching-motion prediction methods in Papers D and F.

projects.title: Co-Founded a Wearable Tech Startup from Concept to Prototype
projects.tagline: Two years building exoskeleton prototypes for assembly-line workers at Science Park Skövde, from user needs to investor pitch.
projects.summary: Co-founded Swe-Ex AB through Science Park Skövde's incubator, developing wearable safety support equipment for assembly-line workers. Led R&D, product iterations, and commercial strategy over 2 years.
projects.challenge: Wearable safety technology for assembly-line workers sits at the intersection of human factors, mechanical design, manufacturing constraints, and commercial viability. Early-stage hardware startups face the challenge of making progress on all four fronts simultaneously with limited resources. Without a structured process for translating user needs into testable design targets, teams burn iterations on the wrong problems.
projects.solution: A structured R&D process within Science Park Skövde's incubator: user needs to design targets to prototype iterations to commercial validation.
whatIDid: Co-founded Swe-Ex AB through Science Park Skövde's incubator, developing exoskeleton-inspired safety support equipment for assembly-line environments
Translated user safety requirements and ergonomic constraints into measurable product targets and drove three full prototype iterations from CAD to physical validation
Conducted market analysis across 10+ industries, managed investor communications, and developed a go-to-market strategy over 2 years in the incubator
impact: Delivered three functional prototype versions with progressively refined ergonomic fit and structural performance
Built a comprehensive competitive landscape and business case informing product direction and investor conversations
Developed direct commercial experience bridging technical capability with product viability, stakeholder communication, and market positioning
projects.learning: Building something physical with real users in a resource-constrained environment teaches prioritization that no simulation study can replicate. The incubator made the connection between technical rigour and commercial viability concrete.

evidence.notes: Startup experience included as a portfolio project alongside the thesis publications.
